text:
sam: Heads up — saw a weird authz pattern after yesterday's KMS rotation. Embeddings evals from the sandbox account succeeded even though the token should have been scoped to chat-only.

maria: :eyes: which token? sandbox eval runner or a user key?

sam: sandbox-eval-runner@infra — token minted by the eval service. Log snippet:
```
2026-03-19T21:12:03Z authz=allow key=sandbox-eval-34 scope=chat.invoke route=/v1/embeddings model=text-embed-32k
```
That scope=chat.invoke is wrong for an embeddings request.

leo: That's alarming. Did the scope migration run? We bumped the per-route enforcement to use KMS-wrapped scope metadata to avoid stale caches.

sam: Yes, rotation happened at 20:58 UTC. My suspicion: rotation changed the KMS key-id we use as cache key so introspection cache missed and fell back to legacy policy which had a permissive rule for sandbox keys.

jamie: Do we have the fallback path logs? audit-bot?

audit-bot: Found traces. Fallback mode triggered for 12 requests between 21:11:55 and 21:12:10. Policy lookup returned fallback=legacy-allowlist.

iris: I dug in. The legacy allowlist rule allowed sandbox-* service accounts full model invocation for evaluation. During the migration we intentionally kept it permissive for QA, but we failed to enforce route scope on fallback.

maria: So sequence: KMS rotation -> cache miss -> fallback to legacy allowlist -> embeddings request matched because route check not applied -> allowed. Correct?

sam: Exactly. Repro steps I ran:
```
# simulate rotated key cache miss
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sandbox-eval-...' -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{input:test}'
# auth decision: fallback -> allow
```

leo: Unacceptable. Even temporary permissive rules must still check route/model scopes. Action items:
1) Immediately disable legacy allowlist fallback for production :lock:
2) Add a preflight introspection on key rotation that invalidates or refreshes cache entries
3) Emit a high-severity audit event when fallback mode is used
4) Patch policy engine to require route-model checks even during fallback

jamie: I'll put a hotfix rolling: revert fallback to false for prod now. Deploy-bot can you run canary?

deploy-bot: Rolling canary to infra-prod-1 (5 nodes). Notifying oncall.

maria: For long-term: add KMS metadata tag origin=rotation-v2 and include kms_key_fingerprint in token bind to avoid cache/identity mismatch.

iris: Also recommend we rotate sandbox tokens and regenerate eval runners. We should TTL tokens shorter for sandbox.

sam: I've created a test that asserts authz=deny for cross-scope requests when fallback is active. Pushed to eng-security/playground branch.

leo: Perf concern: preflight introspection on every request will be costly. Instead: on rotation event, queue async invalidation and a synchronous negative-safe check: if cache miss, deny until introspection completes (fail-closed).

jamie: Agree — fail-closed until explicit migration completed. That blocks sandbox some tests but safer.

maria: Can we also add an eval-only scope (eval.embeddings, eval.chat) so we don't reuse sandbox service account across features?

sam: Good idea. I'll draft RFC for scoping and for a token-introspection endpoint that returns allowed_routes and kms_fingerprint.

iris: For incident notes: severity P2, no user data exfil, but misaligned scopes could allow test models to be invoked. Suggested postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause, impact, rollback, monitoring added.

leo: Who owns postmortem?

sam: I'll own investigation and drafting. Jamie — own rollback/playbook. Maria — own KMS metadata & RFC. Iris — own audit event implementation.

jamie: On it. I'll DM ops to speed up sandbox token rotation.

sam: Thanks all. Will update here with test results and the hotfix PR.

maria: :thumbsup: keep me looped for the RFC review.

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4823

audit-bot: Audit note recorded: incident-2001234567 created by sam at 2026-03-19T21:18:00Z

leo: Good catch. Let's avoid permissive fallbacks in future.
